title: Causatives and phrasal verbs
point: Use have/get something done when someone else does the job, let/make someone do for permission and pressure, and short phrasal verbs where Japanese uses one formal verb.

sentences.ja: 昨日、髪を切ってきたんだ。
sentences.text: I got my hair cut yesterday.
sentences.note: "I cut my hair" sounds like you did it yourself; "got my hair cut" means a stylist did it.

sentences.ja: エアコンを修理してもらわないといけない。
sentences.text: We need to have the air conditioner fixed.

sentences.ja: 親は夜遅くまで外にいさせてくれなかった。
sentences.text: My parents wouldn't let me stay out late.

sentences.ja: 上司に、資料を一から全部作り直させられた。
sentences.text: My boss made me redo the whole thing from scratch.
sentences.note: "Make someone do" has no "to": made me rewrite, not made me to rewrite.

sentences.ja: この問題の解き方がまだ分からない。
sentences.text: I still can't figure out how to solve this problem.
sentences.note: "Figure out" is the everyday verb for working something out; "understand" sounds passive here.

sentences.ja: コピー用紙が切れちゃった。
sentences.text: We've run out of printer paper.

sentences.ja: 歯医者に行くのをずっと先延ばしにしてる。
sentences.text: I keep putting off going to the dentist.

sentences.ja: 週末は、たまったメールを片付けるつもり。
sentences.text: I'm going to catch up on my emails this weekend.

sentences.ja: 誰かもっといいアイデア思いつかない？
sentences.text: Can anyone come up with a better idea?

sentences.ja: 少し考えさせてもらえますか？
sentences.text: Let me think about it for a bit.
sentences.note: "Let me…" is how English asks for a moment; "Please give me time to consider" sounds stiff.
